metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (pricing.cpp) with main() entry point, Dockerfile, and Kubernetes deployment manifests present.
metadata.archetype_justification: No database connections, no cache writes, no message queues. All operations are read-only (HTTP GET returning pricing data from a static flat file). Data is reference-grade product pricing.

findings.title: No structured API interface — CGI returns HTML
findings.description: The application exposes a CGI binary (pricing.cgi) via Apache httpd that accepts HTTP GET requests with query parameters sku and qty. The response is HTML (Content-Type: text/html) meant for human consumption, not a structured REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface.
findings.gap: No structured API interface exists. The only integration path is parsing HTML output from a CGI endpoint — fragile, non-auditable, and unsuitable for agent tool binding.
findings.recommendation: Replace CGI with a modern REST API returning JSON, or add a JSON response mode (Accept: application/json header or format=json parameter) returning structured pricing data.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add a JSON response mode to the CGI endpoint
blocker_remediation.target_state: Proper REST API endpoint returning structured JSON with appropriate HTTP status codes

findings.title: No machine identity authentication
findings.description: The application has no authentication mechanism. The CGI endpoint is accessible to any caller without credentials. No OAuth2, API keys, mTLS, or authorization headers are checked. The Kubernetes service exposes the endpoint on ClusterIP without any authentication layer.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication exists. Any caller can invoke the pricing endpoint without identification or attribution. Agent calls cannot be distinguished from other traffic.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an API Gateway in front of the K8s service with API key authentication or OAuth2 client credentials. Require all callers to present a valid identity.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Deploy API Gateway with API key or OAuth2 client credentials authentication
blocker_remediation.target_state: All API access authenticated via machine identity with individual agent attribution in access logs

findings.title: No scoped permissions model
findings.description: No authorization model exists. The application has no concept of permissions, roles, or access scopes. All callers have identical unrestricted access to all pricing data.
findings.gap: No mechanism to scope agent permissions to specific SKUs, price tiers, or operations.
findings.recommendation: Introduce an API Gateway layer with scoped API keys or OAuth2 scopes that allow differentiating caller access levels.

compensating_controls: Deploy API Gateway with usage plans and scoped API keys
Use Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to restrict which services can reach the pricing endpoint

findings.title: No action-level authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. The application has a single action (lookup price) with no granularity. No authorization infrastructure to support future write operations or differentiated access.
findings.gap: No ABAC, RBAC, or fine-grained permission model. Cannot enforce action-level access control.
findings.recommendation: When adding authentication (AUTH-Q1), implement role-based access with at least read and admin scopes.

compensating_controls: Limit agent scope to read-only at the orchestration layer
API Gateway method-level authorization when write endpoints are introduced

findings.title: No immutable audit logging
findings.description: No audit logging is configured. The application produces no logs of its own. No CloudTrail, CloudWatch, or structured logging is defined anywhere in the repository.
findings.gap: No immutable audit trail for API calls. Cannot determine which agent accessed which pricing data and when.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway with access logging to CloudWatch Logs. Enable CloudTrail for API Gateway events. Configure log retention with S3 object lock for immutability.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only, downgraded from conditional BLOCKER
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Agent scope is read-only (no write operations detected). Audit logging is important but not a deployment blocker for read-only access.
compensating_controls: Apache access logs provide basic request logging at runtime
API Gateway access logging if deployed in front

findings.title: No rate limiting or throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting exists at any layer. The CGI endpoint processes every request without throttling. No API Gateway throttling, no WAF rules, no application-level rate limiting middleware.
findings.gap: No protection against traffic storms from agent bugs or misconfigured retry loops. The service has only 2 replicas with 500m CPU limit — easily exhaustible.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an API Gateway or ingress controller with throttle configuration (e.g., 100 requests/second per caller). Alternatively, add WAF rate-based rules.

compensating_controls: Kubernetes resource limits provide natural backpressure via pod restarts
Network-level rate limiting at the ingress controller if deployed

findings.title: No machine-readable API specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, Smithy model, or any machine-readable API specification exists. The API contract is defined only implicitly in pricing.cpp source code.
findings.gap: Agent tool generation requires manual work. No automated tool binding, no client SDK generation, no contract validation.
findings.recommendation: Create an openapi.yaml file describing the /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi endpoint with query parameters (sku, qty) and response schema.

compensating_controls: Manually author agent tool definitions based on source code analysis
Write an OpenAPI spec describing the current interface

findings.title: No structured error responses
findings.description: All responses return HTTP 200 with HTML regardless of outcome. When a SKU is not found, the response shows Unit: $0.00 with no error differentiation. No structured error codes, no HTTP 4xx/5xx, no machine-readable error body.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish between SKU not found (terminal), rules file unavailable (retriable), and success — all return HTTP 200 with HTML.
findings.recommendation: Return appropriate HTTP status codes (404 for unknown SKU, 500 for file read failure) with a JSON error body containing error code, message, and retryable boolean.

compensating_controls: Agent-side heuristic treating $0.00 unit price as not found signal
Wrapper service translating CGI HTML output into structured JSON

findings.title: No input validation — buffer overflow vulnerabilities
findings.description: The application has NO input validation. The parse_query function uses strcpy without bounds checking — an attacker-controlled SKU parameter can overflow the 64-byte sku buffer. The qty parameter is parsed with atoi which accepts arbitrary strings without validation.
findings.gap: Agents sending malformed payloads (oversized SKU strings, non-numeric qty values) cause undefined behavior including buffer overflows. No structured rejection signals exist for self-correction.
findings.recommendation: Replace strcpy with strncpy with bounds checking. Validate SKU length and qty range. Return structured error responses for invalid input. Consider rewriting in a memory-safe language.

compensating_controls: API Gateway request validation with maximum parameter length constraints
WAF rules to block oversized query strings

findings.title: No schema versioning or API contracts
findings.description: No API versioning, no schema files, no contract documentation, no changelog, no breaking change detection. The CGI URL has no version prefix. No consumer-driven contract tests exist.
findings.gap: Agent tool bindings will break silently if the response format or query parameters change. No mechanism to detect or communicate breaking changes.
findings.recommendation: Introduce URL versioning (e.g., /v1/pricing), document the API contract in an OpenAPI spec, and add contract validation to CI.

compensating_controls: Pin agent tool definitions to specific expected output format
Monitor agent success rates to detect format changes

findings.title: No distributed tracing or structured logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing, no structured logging, no correlation IDs. The CGI binary writes HTML to stdout and produces no logs. No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray instrumentation, no JSON log output.
findings.gap: Agent-initiated requests cannot be traced through the system. Failures are not debuggable.
findings.recommendation: Add structured logging (JSON to stderr) with request_id correlation. Instrument with OpenTelemetry or X-Ray for trace propagation.

compensating_controls: Apache access logs provide basic request-level visibility
API Gateway access logging if deployed

findings.title: No alerting on error rates or latency
findings.description: No alerting is configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration. Only Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes exist.
findings.gap: Target system degradation goes undetected until agents fail. No error rate or latency thresholds configured.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms for HTTP 5xx error rate and p99 latency on the pricing endpoint.

compensating_controls: Kubernetes liveness probe restarts unhealthy pods automatically
Cluster-level monitoring may catch pod restarts

findings.title: No IaC governance for integration surface
findings.description: No IaC defines the integration surface (API gateways, IAM roles, secrets, networking). Kubernetes manifests exist for the deployment itself, but no Terraform, CloudFormation, or CDK defines the surrounding infrastructure.
findings.gap: The agent-facing integration surface is not defined as code. Changes are manual and unauditable.
findings.recommendation: Define the full integration surface in IaC (Terraform or CDK): API Gateway, IAM roles, WAF rules, CloudWatch alarms.

compensating_controls: K8s manifests provide declarative deployment configuration (partial IaC)
GitOps workflow would provide change review on K8s manifests

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline or contract testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodeBuild configuration. The Makefile deploys via scp to a production server. No automated testing or contract validation.
findings.gap: API contract changes cannot be caught before agents are affected. No automated deployment pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Create a CI pipeline that builds the Docker image, runs health checks, and validates the API contract.

compensating_controls: Manual testing before deployment
Kubernetes rolling update provides zero-downtime updates

findings.title: Limited rollback capability
findings.description: Kubernetes deployment provides native rollback via kubectl rollout undo. However, there is no automated rollback trigger, no canary deployment, no progressive delivery configuration.
findings.gap: Rollback exists via Kubernetes native mechanism but is manual with no automated triggers.
findings.recommendation: Configure rollback triggers based on readiness probe failures. Consider Argo Rollouts for automated canary analysis.

compensating_controls: kubectl rollout undo provides immediate rollback
2 replicas ensure continued service during rolling updates

findings.title: No staging or sandbox environment
findings.description: No staging environment. Dockerfile provides local build with a single sample SKU (SAMPLE-SKU|9.99), not production-equivalent data. No environment-specific configurations.
findings.gap: Cannot test agents against realistic pricing data in a safe environment before production deployment.
findings.recommendation: Create a staging namespace with production-equivalent pricing rules. Add Kustomize environment overlay with realistic sample data.

compensating_controls: Docker build provides local testing capability with sample data
Kubernetes namespace isolation could support staging deployment

findings.title: Idempotent write operations — not applicable (read-only)
findings.description: The application has no write operations. All requests are read-only price lookups. Idempotency is inherently satisfied for read operations.
findings.gap: No write operations exist. Question is informational for read-only scope.
findings.recommendation: No action required at current scope. Implement idempotency keys if write endpoints are added.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to INFO: agent_scope=read-only, no write operations present
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: API-Q4 conditional BLOCKER downgrades to INFO under read-only scope because agents do not execute write operations.

findings.title: Response format is HTML — suboptimal for agents
findings.description: API responses are HTML (Content-Type: text/html). The CGI outputs a full HTML page with p tags containing pricing data. This format requires HTML parsing for programmatic consumption.
findings.gap: HTML format requires parsing and is incompatible with direct LLM tool binding.
findings.recommendation: Add a JSON response mode triggered by Accept: application/json header or format=json parameter.

findings.title: No rate limit documentation or headers
findings.description: No rate limits are documented and no rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After) are returned. The system has no concept of rate limiting.
findings.gap: Agents cannot self-throttle based on system capacity signals.
findings.recommendation: When rate limiting is added (STATE-Q5), also return standard rate limit headers in responses.

findings.title: Identity propagation not needed for stateless utility
findings.description: No identity propagation mechanism exists. The system returns public pricing data. Identity context is irrelevant for this stateless utility archetype.
findings.gap: No identity propagation (not needed for public reference data).
findings.recommendation: No action required. Revisit if customer-specific pricing is introduced.

findings.title: No auth surface — identity suspension is consumer responsibility
findings.description: System does not issue or enforce agent identities — suspension is a consumer responsibility. No authentication surface exists, so there are no identities to suspend.
findings.gap: No identities to suspend (dependent on AUTH-Q1 resolution).
findings.recommendation: Design the auth solution (AUTH-Q1) with per-agent-identity revocation capability from the start.

findings.title: Compensation not applicable — stateless read-only service
findings.description: No write operations and no multi-step workflows. Each request is an independent read-only price lookup. Compensation/rollback logic is not applicable for this stateless-utility.
findings.gap: Not applicable for stateless read-only system.
findings.recommendation: No action required.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to INFO: stateless-utility archetype with no write operations
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: STATE-Q1 conditional BLOCKER is calibrated to INFO for stateless-utility archetype — no multi-step write workflows exist.

findings.title: Blast radius limits not applicable — read-only scope
findings.description: No write operations exist. Blast radius limits for write operations are not applicable. The only risk is excessive read traffic, addressed by rate limiting (STATE-Q5).
findings.gap: Not applicable for read-only scope.
findings.recommendation: No action required beyond rate limiting.

findings.title: No sensitive data — reference pricing only
findings.description: System handles product pricing data (SKU codes and unit prices). This is reference/business data, not PII, PHI, or regulated financial records. No sensitive data classification needed.
findings.gap: Not applicable for reference pricing data.
findings.recommendation: No action required. Re-evaluate if customer-specific pricing is introduced.

ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 calibrated to INFO for stateless-utility archetype. System handles transient/public reference data by archetype definition.

findings.gap: Not applicable for reference pricing data.

ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q2 calibrated to INFO for stateless-utility archetype. System handles transient/public reference data with no residency requirements.

findings.description: The system does not handle PII. It processes SKU codes and quantities only — neither of which is personally identifiable information. No logging of user data occurs.
findings.gap: Not applicable for reference pricing data.

findings.title: No automated test coverage
findings.description: No automated tests exist. README acknowledges 'No tests; correctness validated by spot-checking output.' No test files, no test framework.
findings.gap: No test coverage for the agent-consumed API.
findings.recommendation: Add basic integration tests verifying expected pricing responses for known SKUs.

items.summary: Resolve all BLOCKERs (structured API, machine identity) and critical RISK-SAFETY findings (scoped permissions, audit logging, rate limiting) to unblock agent pilots.
Address RISK-QUALITY findings to improve agent effectiveness: machine-readable specs, input validation, observability, CI/CD, and staging environment.
Address INFO-level improvements: JSON response format, rate limit headers, and basic test coverage.

recommended_actions.action: Replace CGI endpoint with REST API returning structured JSON
recommended_actions.rationale: The HTML-only CGI endpoint is the primary integration blocker. A structured JSON API resolves 3 findings simultaneously.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy API Gateway with authentication and rate limiting
recommended_actions.rationale: An API Gateway layer resolves 5 RISK-SAFETY findings plus the authentication BLOCKER in a single infrastructure deployment.

recommended_actions.action: Create CI/CD pipeline with contract testing
recommended_actions.rationale: A CI/CD pipeline with contract tests prevents agent-breaking changes from reaching production.

recommended_actions.action: Add input validation and fix buffer overflow vulnerabilities
recommended_actions.rationale: Buffer overflow vulnerabilities create security risk regardless of agent integration. Input validation also enables structured error responses for agent self-correction.
IaC governance ensures the agent-facing surface is auditable, reviewable, and reproducible.
